name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

# Builds, signs, notarizes, and publishes the macOS and Windows releases, plus
# the updater manifest that makes in-app updates work.
#
# Three jobs build independently (macOS and Windows cannot cross-compile the C
# speech engines), then each publishes its own artifacts to the same tag-based
# release. macOS reuses the exact steps proven in ci.yml's release-macos job,
# including the macOS 15.0 deployment target that keeps ggml-metal's
# @available checks from emitting a dangling ___isPlatformVersionAtLeast
# symbol at link time.
#
# ## Intel
#
# `release-macos-intel` cross-compiles x86_64 from the same Apple Silicon host,
# so there is one macOS build story rather than a separate Intel runner. It is
# `continue-on-error`: Intel is an option we offer, not a promise we gate the
# product on, and it must never be able to block an arm64 or Windows release.
# The publish job treats its absence as normal, and only advertises
# `darwin-x86_64` when the artifact's own recorded architecture says x86_64.
#
# ## What each job produces
#
# - `.app.tar.gz` + `.app.tar.gz.sig` (macOS updater payload)
# - `*.dmg` (macOS human download)
# - `*.nsis.zip` + `*.nsis.zip.sig` (Windows updater payload)
# - `*.exe` (Windows human download)
# - `latest.json` (the updater manifest, merged by the publish job)
#
# ## Signing and notarization
#
# The updater private key (`TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`) signs the update
# payloads. The Apple Developer ID (`APPLE_CERTIFICATE`) signs the app, and
# `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` notarize it.
#
# All four are repository secrets. None of them may be committed. Without the
# Apple credentials the workflow still publishes an unsigned build, because an
# unsigned build that reaches users beats a signed build that never ships; the
# `notarize` step is conditional and says so in the log.
#
# The public half of the updater keypair lives in
# `crates/teletype-desktop/tauri.conf.json` under `plugins.updater.pubkey`.
# That file is safe to commit: the app needs it to verify updates, and it
# cannot be used to sign anything.

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  release-guard:
    name: Release gate - tagged commit must have a green CI run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    env:
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      ALLOW_NO_UPDATER: ${{ vars.ALLOW_NO_UPDATER }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Verify the tagged commit has a successful CI run
        # F-05: a tag must never be able to publish a commit CI never validated.
        # Query this commit's CI runs with the workflow token.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          RUNS="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs?head_sha=${GITHUB_SHA}&per_page=100")"
          GOOD="$(printf '%s' "$RUNS" | jq -r --arg w "CI" \
            '.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $w and .status == "completed" and .conclusion == "success") | .id' \
            | head -n1)"
          if [ -z "$GOOD" ] || [ "$GOOD" = "null" ]; then
            echo "::error::No successful CI run for commit ${GITHUB_SHA}. Refusing to build or publish a release from an unverified commit."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "CI run ${GOOD} succeeded for ${GITHUB_SHA}."
      - name: Verify the tagged commit is reachable from main or a release branch
        # A tag is pushed independently of any branch, so the checkout here is
        # the tag commit, which sits ABOVE the branch tip. `git branch -r
        # --contains` only sees the checkout's local remote-tracking refs and
        # finds no branch containing a tag that is ahead of them, so it fails
        # for every tag. Use the API's compare endpoint instead: it checks
        # reachability against the live remote branch, which is what we mean.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          FOUND=""
          for BRANCH in main release/v0.2.17 release/v0.2.16 release/v0.2.15; do
            STATUS="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/compare/${BRANCH}...${GITHUB_SHA}" \
              --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo "missing")"
            echo "compare ${BRANCH}...${GITHUB_SHA} => ${STATUS}"
            if [ "$STATUS" = "behind" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "identical" ]; then
              FOUND="$BRANCH"
              break
            fi
          done
          if [ -z "$FOUND" ]; then
            echo "::error::Commit ${GITHUB_SHA} is not reachable from main or a release/* branch. Refusing to build or publish a release from an unverified commit."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Commit ${GITHUB_SHA} is reachable from ${FOUND}."
      - name: Preflight - updater signing posture
        # F-04 makes a zero-platform updater manifest a hard failure, but the
        # publish job only discovers it after the arm64, Intel and Windows build
        # jobs have all finished. That failure is not a risk in this case, it is
        # certain: the build jobs clear the signing env when the key is absent,
        # so no `.sig` artifact is ever produced, so every manifest entry is
        # skipped, so `platforms` is empty. Catch it here, on a cheap Linux
        # runner in seconds, instead of after a full set of macOS build minutes.
        #
        # The Apple certificate and notarization credentials are deliberately
        # not gated: the header of this file documents that an unsigned build
        # that reaches users beats a signed build that never ships.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          KEY="${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
          KEY_TRIMMED="$(printf '%s' "$KEY" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
          ALLOW="${ALLOW_NO_UPDATER:-}"
          if [ -z "$KEY_TRIMMED" ]; then
            if [ "$ALLOW" = "true" ]; then
              echo "::notice::No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY and ALLOW_NO_UPDATER=true. This release publishes unsigned with a zero-platform updater manifest (in-app updates off) and stays a pre-release."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "::error::No usable TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY secret (absent or empty) and the repository variable ALLOW_NO_UPDATER is not 'true'. All three build jobs would run and then the publish job would refuse the release for having a zero-platform manifest. Either add the secret, or set ALLOW_NO_UPDATER=true to say you mean to ship an unsigned pre-release."
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! printf '%s\n' "$KEY" | head -1 | grep -q '^#'; then
            echo "::error::TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY is missing its '#' comment header line. The key must be pasted in full, including the comment line at the top (tauri signer generate)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Updater signing key present and well-formed; this release can produce a signed updater manifest."

  release-macos:
    name: Build & publish macOS release
    needs: [release-guard]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    env:
      # ggml-metal's ggml-metal-device.m uses @available(macOS 15.0) checks.
      # Compiling below 15.0 emits a strong reference to
      # ___isPlatformVersionAtLeast that the final link cannot resolve.
      # 15.0 makes clang fold the check away and still covers the 10.15+
      # std::filesystem requirement. whisper-rs-sys forwards any CMAKE_* env
      # var to CMake, so set the deployment target there.
      CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: "15.0"
      # The real source of the too-low floor. The `cc` crate reads
      # MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET (not CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET) and, when it
      # is unset, emits its own fallback of 10.13 straight into the
      # CMAKE_C_FLAGS/CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS it hands to every CMake build script.
      # Set it so 10.13 never reaches the command line at all, instead of
      # relying on a later -mmacosx-version-min winning over it.
      MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: "15.0"
      # transcribe-cpp-sys does NOT forward CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET to CMake
      # (unlike whisper-rs-sys); without it its vendored ggml C++ compiles with
      # an empty deployment target, below 10.15, where std::filesystem's
      # fs::path is marked unavailable and the build fails. Its build.rs does
      # forward TRANSCRIBE_CMAKE_ARGS, so pass the floor through there.
      TRANSCRIBE_CMAKE_ARGS: "-DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0"
      # Match the final Rust link to the same deployment target.
      RUSTFLAGS: "-C link-arg=-mmacosx-version-min=15.0"
      # sccache: cache C/C++/Rust object files across runs. The whisper.cpp +
      # ggml compilation is the expensive part and is deterministic, so a warm
      # cache cuts the Tauri build from ~7 min to ~2 min.
      SCCACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.sccache-cache
      CARGO_TARGET_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.cargo-target-cache
      # Consumed by `cargo tauri build` to sign the updater payload. The public
      # key is already pinned in tauri.conf.json.
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
      # Tauri's Apple signing + notarization. Optional: see the header.
      APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
      APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
      APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
      APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD }}
      APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Sync version to the tag
        # Tauri bakes the version from tauri.conf.json (and the workspace
        # Cargo.toml) into the DMG/EXE filenames and the app's reported
        # version, NOT from the git tag. If those drift from the tag, the
        # release assets are misnamed (e.g. a v0.2.4 tag ships
        # Teletype_0.2.2_aarch64.dmg). Rewrite both to the tag so the
        # artifact names and the app's version always match the release.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          VER="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          echo "Syncing version to $VER"
          sed -i '' "s/^version = \".*\"/version = \"$VER\"/" Cargo.toml
          python3 -c "import json; p='crates/teletype-desktop/tauri.conf.json'; d=json.load(open(p)); d['version']='$VER'; json.dump(d, open(p,'w'), indent=2); open(p,'a').write(chr(10))"
          grep '^version' Cargo.toml
          grep '"version"' crates/teletype-desktop/tauri.conf.json
      - name: Preflight - Apple certificate secret
        # A malformed APPLE_CERTIFICATE (not base64, or not a .p12) fails deep
        # inside the Tauri build with "failed to import keychain certificate"
        # after ~20 minutes of compilation. Check it first, in seconds.
        # NOTE: the failing branch must `exit 1` at top level, not inside a
        # `{ ... }` group after `||` — that only exits the subshell and lets
        # the step (and the 20-minute build) continue.
        #
        # A secret that exists in the repo but is an empty string (or
        # whitespace-only) is treated the same as an absent one: Tauri's
        # `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` handling does not distinguish them, and an
        # empty value makes `security import` fail exactly like a malformed
        # one. Trim before deciding whether to sign at all.
        run: |
          CERT="${APPLE_CERTIFICATE:-}"
          CERT_TRIMMED="$(printf '%s' "$CERT" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
          if [ -z "$CERT_TRIMMED" ]; then
            echo "No usable APPLE_CERTIFICATE secret (absent or empty): building unsigned (expected until the secret is added)."
            exit 0
          fi
          if ! echo "$CERT" | base64 -d > /tmp/cert.p12 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::APPLE_CERTIFICATE is not valid base64. It must be the base64 of a .p12 file (see docs/signing-and-updates.md)."
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! openssl pkcs12 -in /tmp/cert.p12 -nokeys -passin pass:"${APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD}" -noout 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::APPLE_CERTIFICATE is not a readable .p12 (wrong APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD, or not a .p12 export)."
            exit 1
          fi
          rm -f /tmp/cert.p12
          echo "Apple certificate secret looks valid."
      - name: Preflight - updater signing key
        # A minisign key pasted without its "# comment" header line fails with
        # "Missing comment in secret key" at bundle time. Check in seconds.
        # Same empty-string trap as the Apple certificate: an empty-but-present
        # secret must be treated as absent, or Tauri tries to decode it and
        # fails at bundle time.
        run: |
          KEY="${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
          KEY_TRIMMED="$(printf '%s' "$KEY" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
          if [ -z "$KEY_TRIMMED" ]; then
            echo "No usable TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY secret (absent or empty): updater artifacts will not be signed (expected until the secret is added)."
            exit 0
          fi
          if ! printf '%s\n' "$KEY" | head -1 | grep -q '^#'; then
            echo "::error::TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY is missing its '#' comment header line. The key must be pasted in full, including the comment line at the top (tauri signer generate)."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Updater signing key looks valid."
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: "1.90"
          components: "rustfmt"
      - name: Install sccache
        run: |
          brew install sccache 2>/dev/null || true
          sccache --show-stats || true
      - name: Cache sccache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.sccache-cache
          key: sccache-macos-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            sccache-macos-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: Cache cargo target
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.cargo-target-cache
          key: cargo-target-macos-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            cargo-target-macos-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - name: Install tauri-cli
        # Pin to a tauri-cli that builds on the pinned Rust 1.88 toolchain.
        # tauri-cli must match the tauri crate version in Cargo.lock.
        run: |
          if ! cargo tauri --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "2.12.0"; then
            cargo install tauri-cli --version "2.12.0" --locked
          fi
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json
      - name: Install UI deps
        run: cd ui && npm ci
      - name: Check third-party notices sync
        run: bash scripts/check-notices.sh
      - name: Build llama-server (Metal, static)
        run: |
          ./scripts/build-llama-server.sh
      - name: Build Tauri app
        # Signs the app (when APPLE_CERTIFICATE is present), signs the updater
        # payload, and notarizes. `createUpdaterArtifacts: true` in
        # tauri.conf.json is what produces the .app.tar.gz + .sig pair.
        #
        # An empty-but-present secret is treated as absent (see the preflight
        # step above): Tauri does not distinguish the two, and an empty value
        # fails `security import` / minisign decode exactly like a malformed
        # one. Clear the vars for this step when the preflight found nothing
        # usable, so Tauri takes its unsigned path instead of trying to sign
        # with an empty key.
        run: |
          if [ -z "$(printf '%s' "${APPLE_CERTIFICATE:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "No usable APPLE_CERTIFICATE: clearing signing env for an unsigned build."
            unset APPLE_CERTIFICATE APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD APPLE_ID APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD APPLE_TEAM_ID
          fi
          # Updater artifacts are a separate concern from Apple signing, and
          # clearing the key env is not enough to skip them. tauri.conf.json
          # sets bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts: true, so Tauri builds the
          # .app.tar.gz, finds the updater pubkey it can see, has no private
          # key to sign it with, and aborts *after* bundling:
          #
          #     Finished 2 bundles at: .../Teletype.app (39.28 MiB)
          #                               .../Teletype_0.2.2_aarch64.dmg (20.20 MiB)
          #     Bundling .../Teletype.app.tar.gz (updater) (19.59 MiB)
          #     Error A public key has been found, but no private key.
          #
          # That is a ~7-minute compile discarded at the last step, and it is
          # how every release attempt so far died. Turn the artifacts off for
          # this build via the CLI rather than editing tauri.conf.json, so a
          # release that does have a key still produces updater payloads and
          # their .sig files with no change to the committed config.
          if [ -z "$(printf '%s' "${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "No usable TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: clearing updater-signing env and skipping updater artifacts."
            unset TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD
            cargo tauri build --bundles app,dmg \
              --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          else
            cargo tauri build --bundles app,dmg
          fi
      - name: Installer smoke (self-test)
        # Plan §9.2: the exact binary that ships must pass a headless
        # pipeline run (model loads, hello.wav transcribes, text pipeline
        # runs, exit 0). Runs the freshly built release binary with the
        # default macOS model staged via TELETYPE_SELF_TEST_MODELS, the same
        # seam the self_test unit tests use. Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 pipeline
        # failure, 2 model missing. The binary self-times-out at 120 s.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          BIN="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/release/teletype
          test -f "$BIN"
          MODELS="$(mktemp -d)"/models
          mkdir -p "$MODELS"
          # Must match `PARAKEET_BASE_URL` in teletype-speech/src/catalog.rs:
          # this ggml build lives in ggml-org/parakeet-GGUF, not the whisper.cpp
          # repo, and the old URL 404'd the whole release.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 \
            -o "$MODELS/ggml-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-q8_0.bin" \
            "https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/parakeet-GGUF/resolve/main/ggml-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-q8_0.bin"
          export TELETYPE_SELF_TEST_MODELS="$MODELS"
          # Pin the row that was staged: without it the smoke follows the
          # platform default, which on Apple Silicon resolves to the Core ML
          # repo that this artifact directory will never contain.
          export TELETYPE_SELF_TEST_MODEL=parakeet-tdt-v3
          set +e
          "$BIN" --self-test
          CODE=$?
          set -e
          if [ "$CODE" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::--self-test exited $CODE (0=ok, 1=pipeline failure, 2=missing model)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Installer smoke passed."
      - name: Report signing state
        # `env` is not available in a step-level `if`, so branch in the shell.
        # An unsigned build is published deliberately (see the header): a build
        # that reaches users beats a signed build that never ships.
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "${APPLE_CERTIFICATE:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "Apple signing credentials present: the app is signed and notarized."
            spctl --assess --type execute --verbose \
              "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/release/bundle/macos/*.app
          else
            echo "::warning::No usable APPLE_CERTIFICATE secret (absent or empty). Publishing an UNSIGNED build."
            echo "::warning::macOS Gatekeeper will block first launch until the user"
            echo "::warning::right-clicks the app and opens it. Add the signing"
            echo "::warning::secrets before the next tag to ship a clean install."
          fi
      - name: Record the architecture
        # The updater manifest is assembled in the publish job, which sees both
        # macOS payloads and cannot tell them apart by filename: both are
        # Teletype.app.tar.gz. A marker written here, by the job that actually
        # built the binary, is what lets publish refuse to advertise a payload
        # under the wrong platform key. Getting this wrong is not cosmetic: a
        # `darwin-x86_64` entry pointing at an arm64 payload installs, passes
        # signature verification, and then refuses to open.
        #
        # The marker says `aarch64`, not `arm64`. `file` prints `arm64`; the
        # updater platform key, the Rust target triple and llama.cpp all say
        # `aarch64`. This writes the name the manifest keys off, and uses
        # `file` only to prove the binary really is that architecture.
        #
        # Every path here comes from $CARGO_TARGET_DIR, never from a literal.
        # Tauri honours CARGO_TARGET_DIR, and this job sets it to
        # `.cargo-target-cache`, so the build really lands in
        # `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/release/...`. It is also a workspace build:
        # teletype-desktop is a member of the root workspace, so it shares the
        # root `target/` and has no `crates/teletype-desktop/target/` of its
        # own. A hardcoded path is therefore wrong twice over, and the
        # `test -f` below turns that into a red step after ~20 minutes.
        run: |
          BIN="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/release/teletype
          test -f "$BIN"
          file "$BIN" | grep -q "arm64" || {
            echo "::error::the aarch64 build is not arm64: $(file -b "$BIN")"
            exit 1
          }
          echo aarch64 > "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/release/bundle/macos/ARCH
          cat "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/release/bundle/macos/ARCH
      - name: Zip the .app bundle
        # A GitHub release asset has to be a *file*. A macOS `.app` is a
        # directory, so the `dist/**/*.app` glob in the release step has never
        # matched anything: v0.2.2 shipped the DMG and the Windows installer,
        # and silently dropped a 39 MiB app bundle that had been sitting in the
        # build artifact the whole time. Zip it so it can ship.
        #
        # `ditto`, not `zip -r`: an app bundle carries symlinks inside
        # Frameworks and executable bits on the binary, and plain `zip` gets
        # both wrong in ways that only show up as a broken app on someone
        # else's machine. `ditto -c -k --keepParent` is what Tauri's own
        # bundle_dmg.sh uses, and it is the format Apple documents for
        # distributing an app outside the App Store.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          B="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/release/bundle/macos
          APP="$(find "$B" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.app' -type d | head -1)"
          if [ -z "$APP" ]; then
            echo "::error::no .app directory under $B"
            exit 1
          fi
          rm -f "$B"/*.app.zip
          ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$APP" "$B/$(basename "$APP").zip"
          ls -la "$B"/*.app.zip
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: macos-release
          path: |
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/release/bundle/macos/ARCH
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/release/bundle/macos/*.app.zip
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/release/bundle/macos/*.app.tar.gz
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/release/bundle/macos/*.app.tar.gz.sig
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error

  # The Intel build is a second macOS job rather than a universal binary.
  # A universal build would need one llama-server that runs on both
  # architectures, and llama.cpp is compiled per architecture, so the "universal"
  # option is really "two builds, one bundle", with a bundle that is twice the
  # size and cannot be code-signed as a single file. Two separate artifacts is
  # the smaller, simpler, and separately-updatable answer.
  #
  # An Intel Mac has no Neural Engine, so Parakeet runs on the CPU, and
  # llama.cpp's Metal backend on Intel integrated graphics is much slower than on
  # Apple Silicon. The build is correct and installable; the performance is not
  # competitive. The job is non-blocking for that reason: Intel support is an
  # option, not a promise, and it must not be able to block an arm64 release.
  release-macos-intel:
    name: Build & publish macOS Intel (x86_64) release
    needs: [release-guard]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    continue-on-error: true
    env:
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
      APPLE_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE }}
      APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
      APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
      APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD }}
      APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
      # Cross-compile flags, shared with ci.yml's macos-intel-build. clang is a
      # universal binary so only `-arch` differs between the two builds.
      CC_x86_64_apple_darwin: clang
      CXX_x86_64_apple_darwin: clang++
      CFLAGS_x86_64_apple_darwin: "-arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0"
      CXXFLAGS_x86_64_apple_darwin: "-arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0"
      CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES: x86_64
      CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: "15.0"
      # See the arm64 job: `cc` reads this var, not CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET,
      # and injects its own 10.13 fallback into the CMake flags when unset.
      MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: "15.0"
      # Same transcribe-cpp-sys gap as the arm64 job: its build.rs does not
      # forward CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, so pin the floor via the
      # TRANSCRIBE_CMAKE_ARGS passthrough or its vendored ggml C++ fails below
      # the 10.15 std::filesystem requirement.
      TRANSCRIBE_CMAKE_ARGS: "-DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0"
      RUSTFLAGS: "-C link-arg=-mmacosx-version-min=15.0"
      # Consumed by scripts/build-llama-server.sh.
      TELETYPE_TARGET_TRIPLE: x86_64-apple-darwin
      # sccache + cargo cache (same strategy as the arm64 job).
      SCCACHE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.sccache-cache
      CARGO_TARGET_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.cargo-target-cache
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Sync version to the tag
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          VER="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          echo "Syncing version to $VER"
          sed -i '' "s/^version = \".*\"/version = \"$VER\"/" Cargo.toml
          python3 -c "import json; p='crates/teletype-desktop/tauri.conf.json'; d=json.load(open(p)); d['version']='$VER'; json.dump(d, open(p,'w'), indent=2); open(p,'a').write(chr(10))"
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: "1.90"
      - name: Add the x86_64 target
        run: rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin
      - name: Install sccache
        run: |
          brew install sccache 2>/dev/null || true
      - name: Cache sccache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.sccache-cache
          key: sccache-macos-intel-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            sccache-macos-intel-
      - name: Cache cargo target
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.cargo-target-cache
          key: cargo-target-macos-intel-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            cargo-target-macos-intel-
      - name: Install tauri-cli
        run: |
          if ! cargo tauri --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q "2.12.0"; then
            cargo install tauri-cli --version "2.12.0" --locked
          fi
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json
      - name: Install UI deps
        run: cd ui && npm ci
      - name: Check third-party notices sync
        run: bash scripts/check-notices.sh
      - name: Build llama-server (x86_64)
        run: ./scripts/build-llama-server.sh
      - name: Build Tauri app (x86_64)
        # Same empty-secret handling as the arm64 job: an empty-but-present
        # APPLE_CERTIFICATE/TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY is treated as absent and
        # cleared before the build, so Tauri takes its unsigned path.
        run: |
          if [ -z "$(printf '%s' "${APPLE_CERTIFICATE:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "No usable APPLE_CERTIFICATE: clearing signing env for an unsigned Intel build."
            unset APPLE_CERTIFICATE APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD APPLE_ID APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD APPLE_TEAM_ID
          fi
          # Same updater-artifact trap as the arm64 job: see the long note
          # there. Clearing the key env does not stop Tauri from trying to
          # build and sign the updater payload.
          if [ -z "$(printf '%s' "${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "No usable TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: clearing updater-signing env and skipping updater artifacts."
            unset TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD
            cargo tauri build --target x86_64-apple-darwin --bundles app,dmg \
              --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          else
            cargo tauri build --target x86_64-apple-darwin --bundles app,dmg
          fi
      - name: Verify the binary really is x86_64
        # Without this, a mis-set flag would publish an arm64 app under the
        # x86_64 name: it would install, verify its own signature, and then
        # refuse to launch on the very machines this job exists to serve.
        run: |
          BIN="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/teletype
          test -f "$BIN" || { echo "no binary at $BIN"; exit 1; }
          file "$BIN"
          file "$BIN" | grep -q "x86_64" || {
            echo "::error::expected an x86_64 binary, got: $(file -b "$BIN")"
            exit 1
          }
      - name: Report signing state
        run: |
          if [ -n "$(printf '%s' "${APPLE_CERTIFICATE:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
            echo "Apple signing credentials present: the Intel app is signed and notarized."
            spctl --assess --type execute --verbose \
              "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos/*.app
          else
            echo "::warning::No usable APPLE_CERTIFICATE secret (absent or empty). Publishing an UNSIGNED Intel build."
          fi
      - name: Record the architecture
        run: |
          BIN="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/teletype
          test -f "$BIN"
          file "$BIN" | grep -q "x86_64" || {
            echo "::error::the x86_64 build is not x86_64: $(file -b "$BIN")"
            exit 1
          }
          B="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos
          echo x86_64 > "$B/ARCH"
          cat "$B/ARCH"
      - name: Give the Intel assets distinct names
        # Both builds produce a file called Teletype.app.tar.gz. GitHub release
        # assets are keyed by name, so uploading both would either fail or
        # silently keep one architecture, which is the exact failure this job is
        # meant to prevent. The arm64 assets keep their existing names, so this
        # release does not change for Apple Silicon users at all.
        #
        # Renaming the .app *directory* is safe: Finder, Launchpad and Spotlight
        # read CFBundleName from the bundle's own Info.plist, not the name of
        # the enclosing folder, and the binary is still at Contents/MacOS.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          B="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos
          mv "$B/Teletype.app" "$B/Teletype-x86_64.app"
          for f in "$B"/Teletype.app.tar.gz "$B"/Teletype.app.tar.gz.sig; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            mv "$f" "${f/Teletype.app/Teletype-x86_64.app}"
          done
          ls -1 "$B"
      - name: Zip the Intel .app bundle
        # Same reason as the arm64 job: a release asset must be a file, and a
        # `.app` is a directory, so without this the Intel build contributes
        # no downloadable macOS artifact at all. v0.2.2 shipped nothing for
        # Intel for exactly this reason.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          B="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos
          APP="$(find "$B" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.app' -type d | head -1)"
          if [ -z "$APP" ]; then
            echo "::error::no .app directory under $B"
            exit 1
          fi
          rm -f "$B"/*.app.zip
          ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent "$APP" "$B/$(basename "$APP").zip"
          ls -la "$B"/*.app.zip
      - name: Name the Intel DMG unambiguously
        # Tauri suffixes the DMG with the architecture (the arm64 job produced
        # `Teletype_0.2.2_aarch64.dmg`), but this job does not rely on that: it
        # renames the file to a name that says x86_64 whatever the bundler
        # called it. The two macOS DMGs share one release, and GitHub keys
        # assets by name, so a collision would silently drop one architecture.
        # The publish job also fails on duplicate names, which is the backstop.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          D="$CARGO_TARGET_DIR"/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg
          DMG="$(find "$D" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.dmg' -type f | head -1)"
          if [ -z "$DMG" ]; then
            echo "::error::no .dmg under $D; the Intel job now builds --bundles app,dmg"
            exit 1
          fi
          mv "$DMG" "$D/Teletype-x86_64.dmg"
          ls -la "$D"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: macos-release-intel
          path: |
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos/ARCH
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos/*.app.zip
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos/*.app.tar.gz
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos/*.app.tar.gz.sig
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error

  release-windows:
    name: Build & publish Windows release
    needs: [release-guard]
    runs-on: windows-latest
    env:
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
      # This job has always cached .cargo-target-cache, but it never told
      # cargo to use it, so the cache was written and then ignored: cargo built
      # into the workspace default `target/` and the cache step saved a
      # directory nothing read. Setting it here makes the cache real and gives
      # the upload paths below a single source of truth for where the bundle
      # lands (see the arm64 job for why a literal path is wrong twice over).
      CARGO_TARGET_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/.cargo-target-cache
    steps:
      - name: Preflight - updater signing key
        # A minisign key pasted without its "# comment" header line fails with
        # "Missing comment in secret key" at bundle time, after a ~30-minute
        # build. Check in seconds. NOTE: use `throw`, not `Write-Error` — the
        # default shell is PowerShell, where Write-Error is non-terminating
        # and would let the build continue past the failure.
        #
        # An empty-but-present secret is treated as absent (same trap as the
        # macOS jobs): `$env:TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` is non-null when the
        # secret exists but is an empty string, so the null check alone would
        # miss it and the build would try to decode an empty key.
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $key = $env:TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY
          if ($null -eq $key -or -not ($key.Trim())) {
            Write-Host "No usable TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY (absent or empty): updater artifacts will not be signed."
            exit 0
          }
          $firstLine = ($key -split "`n")[0].Trim()
          if ($firstLine -notmatch '^#') {
            throw "TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY is missing its '#' comment header line. Paste the key in full, including the comment line at the top (tauri signer generate)."
          }
          Write-Host "Updater signing key looks valid."
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Sync version to the tag
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ver = $env:GITHUB_REF_NAME -replace '^v', ''
          Write-Host "Syncing version to $ver"
          (Get-Content Cargo.toml) -replace '^version = ".*"', "version = `"$ver`"" | Set-Content Cargo.toml
          $p = 'crates\teletype-desktop\tauri.conf.json'
          $d = Get-Content $p -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
          $d.version = $ver
          $d | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 32 | Set-Content $p
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          toolchain: "1.90"
      - name: Install sccache
        run: choco install sccache -y
      - name: Cache sccache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.sccache-cache
          key: sccache-windows-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            sccache-windows-
      - name: Cache cargo target
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.cargo-target-cache
          key: cargo-target-windows-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            cargo-target-windows-
      - name: Install tauri-cli
        run: |
          if (-not (cargo tauri --version 2>$null | Select-String "2.9.3")) {
            cargo install tauri-cli --version "2.12.0" --locked
          }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json
      - name: Install UI deps
        run: cd ui; npm ci
      - name: Build llama-server (CPU, static)
        # Windows has no Metal; build llama-server with the CPU backend and
        # static linking so the NSIS bundle carries a single self-contained
        # executable. The app calls it over 127.0.0.1 HTTP, so no TLS is needed.
        run: |
          git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp llama.cpp
          cd llama.cpp
          git checkout --detach f95b0d95394d5e311ba8228689972843178c5e28
          cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_APP=OFF
          cmake --build build --config Release --target llama-server
          # llama.cpp's server target lands in build\bin\Release (not build\Release).
          # cwd is <repo>/llama.cpp, so ..\ is the repo root.
          #
          # The destination must be the path tauri.conf.json actually maps
          # ("binaries/llama-server", no extension). Copying to
          # `llama-server.exe` put the real binary *next to* the mapped path,
          # so the bundle shipped the 74-byte placeholder committed there and
          # every Windows user who selected a local polish model got
          # "llama-server binary not found. Run scripts/build-llama-server.sh".
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path '..\crates\teletype-desktop\binaries' -Force | Out-Null
          $dest = '..\crates\teletype-desktop\binaries\llama-server.exe'
          Copy-Item build/bin/Release/llama-server.exe $dest
          # The resource map has no extension, so mirror the built binary onto
          # it as well. Keeping both means either mapping resolves.
          Copy-Item $dest '..\crates\teletype-desktop\binaries\llama-server'
          # The destination is no longer a committed placeholder (it is a build
          # artifact, see .gitignore and scripts/check-no-built-binaries.sh), so
          # this is checking the copy we just made rather than catching a
          # stale one. Keep it anyway: a short file here is a truncated or
          # wrong-architecture build, and shipping that is worse than failing.
          if ((Get-Item '..\crates\teletype-desktop\binaries\llama-server').Length -lt 1000000) {
            Write-Error "llama-server copy is under 1 MB; refusing to ship it"
            exit 1
          }
      - name: Build Tauri app (NSIS)
        # Produces the .exe, the .nsis.zip updater payload, and its signature.
        # An empty-but-present TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY is treated as absent
        # (same trap as the macOS jobs): clear it before the build so Tauri
        # takes its unsigned path instead of failing to decode an empty key.
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $key = $env:TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY
          if ($null -eq $key -or -not ($key.Trim())) {
            Write-Host "No usable TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: clearing updater-signing env and skipping updater artifacts."
            Remove-Item Env:TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            Remove-Item Env:TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            # Same updater-artifact trap as the macOS jobs: tauri.conf.json
            # sets bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts: true, so clearing the key
            # env is not enough. Tauri bundles the .nsis.zip, sees the
            # updater pubkey, has no private key, and aborts after a
            # ~30-minute build with "A public key has been found, but no
            # private key". Overridden at the CLI so a signed release still
            # produces updater payloads unchanged.
            cargo tauri build --bundles nsis --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          } else {
            cargo tauri build --bundles nsis
          }
      - name: Installer smoke (self-test)
        # Same gate as the macOS job (plan §9.2): the shipping binary must
        # run the pipeline headlessly and exit 0.
        #
        # Windows has no Whisper or ggml Parakeet: whisper-rs, parakeet-sys and
        # parakeet-cpp-sys are macOS-only dependencies, so the only engine this
        # binary can load is sherpa-onnx. Stage the Windows default itself
        # (sherpa-parakeet-v3-int8, the row default_speech_model_id() resolves
        # to here) and pin the smoke to it. The archive extracts to
        # <models>/sherpa/<archive stem>, which is the path
        # SpeechModel::provider_path builds for the sherpa engine.
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $bin = Join-Path $env:CARGO_TARGET_DIR "release\teletype.exe"
          if (-not (Test-Path $bin)) { throw "release binary not found: $bin" }
          $models = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "selftest-models"
          $sherpa = Join-Path $models "sherpa"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $sherpa -Force | Out-Null
          $archive = "sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8.tar.bz2"
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases/download/asr-models/$archive" -OutFile (Join-Path $models $archive) -UseBasicParsing
          tar -xjf (Join-Path $models $archive) -C $sherpa
          if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $sherpa "sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8"))) { throw "sherpa archive did not extract to the path the catalog expects" }
          Remove-Item (Join-Path $models $archive)
          $env:TELETYPE_SELF_TEST_MODELS = $models
          $env:TELETYPE_SELF_TEST_MODEL = "sherpa-parakeet-v3-int8"
          & $bin --self-test
          $code = $LASTEXITCODE
          if ($code -ne 0) {
            Write-Error "--self-test exited $code (0=ok, 1=pipeline failure, 2=missing model)"
            exit 1
          }
          Write-Host "Installer smoke passed."
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: windows-release
          path: |
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/release/bundle/nsis/*.exe
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/release/bundle/nsis/*.nsis.zip
            ${{ env.CARGO_TARGET_DIR }}/release/bundle/nsis/*.nsis.zip.sig
          if-no-files-found: error

  # Publishes everything to one release and writes the merged updater manifest.
  #
  # The manifest has to be built here, not in the build jobs, because it must
  # list both platforms: each job only knows about its own. A manifest missing
  # one platform means that platform's users can never be offered an update.
  verify-release:
    name: Verify the published release + updater manifest
    needs: [publish]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # `gh release edit` below mutates the release (pre-release flag,
    # "latest" marker), so this job needs contents: write. It is the only
    # job that edits the published release.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Download the just-published latest.json
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -o latest.json \
            "https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/releases/download/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}/latest.json"
      - name: Check the published updater manifest
        # The zero-platform case is not a failure here: the publish job only
        # publishes a zero-platform manifest when ALLOW_NO_UPDATER=true, and
        # that release must stay a pre-release. The check records which path
        # this release took, in a file the promote step reads.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          VERSION="${TAG#v}"
          python3 - "$VERSION" latest.json <<'PY'
          import json, sys, urllib.request

          version, path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
          with open(path) as fh:
              manifest = json.load(fh)
          problems = []
          if manifest.get("version") != version:
              problems.append(f"version {manifest.get('version')!r} does not equal tag {version!r}")
          platforms = manifest.get("platforms") or {}
          for key, entry in sorted(platforms.items()):
              if not (entry or {}).get("signature"):
                  problems.append(f"{key}: empty signature")
              url = (entry or {}).get("url") or ""
              if not url:
                  problems.append(f"{key}: missing download url")
                  continue
              req = urllib.request.Request(url, method="HEAD")
              try:
                  with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
                      if resp.status != 200:
                          problems.append(f"{key}: download url returned HTTP {resp.status}")
              except Exception as exc:
                  problems.append(f"{key}: download url {url} not reachable ({exc})")
          if problems:
              for problem in problems:
                  print(f"::error::{problem}")
              raise SystemExit(1)
          with open("manifest-path.txt", "w") as fh:
              if platforms:
                  fh.write("signed\n")
                  print(f"published updater manifest OK: version {version}, platforms {sorted(platforms)}")
              else:
                  fh.write("allow-no-updater\n")
                  print("published updater manifest has zero platforms. This release was published under ALLOW_NO_UPDATER=true and must stay a pre-release.")
          PY
      - name: Promote the release to latest
        # Only reached when the post-publish verification passed (the job
        # `needs: [publish]`, and the check above exits 1 otherwise).
        #
        # A release published under ALLOW_NO_UPDATER=true (no updater signing
        # key, zero-platform manifest) must stay a pre-release: it has no
        # updater payload for anyone, so it must never be "latest" and the
        # updater must never read its manifest.
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PATH_CASE="$(cat manifest-path.txt)"
          if [ "$PATH_CASE" = "allow-no-updater" ]; then
            echo "ALLOW_NO_UPDATER path: release stays a pre-release and is not marked latest."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "Signed path: promoting the release to latest and clearing the pre-release flag."
          gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --prerelease=false --latest

  publish:
    name: Publish release & updater manifest
    needs: [release-macos, release-macos-intel, release-windows]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
      ALLOW_NO_UPDATER: ${{ vars.ALLOW_NO_UPDATER }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: dist
      - name: Assemble the updater manifest
        # Uses the endpoint from tauri.conf.json rather than repeating it here,
        # so the two cannot drift.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          base="https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/releases/download/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          KEY="${TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
          KEY_TRIMMED="$(printf '%s' "$KEY" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
          if [ -n "$KEY_TRIMMED" ]; then KEY_PRESENT="true"; else KEY_PRESENT="false"; fi
          ALLOW="${ALLOW_NO_UPDATER:-}"
          if [ "$ALLOW" = "true" ]; then ALLOW_TRUE="true"; else ALLOW_TRUE="false"; fi
          python3 - "$version" "$base" "$KEY_PRESENT" "$ALLOW_TRUE" <<'PY'
          import datetime, glob, hashlib, json, os, sys

          version, base = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
          key_present = sys.argv[3] == "true"
          allow = sys.argv[4] == "true"
          platforms = {}

          # One entry per (payload, signature) pair actually present. A macOS
          # build can legitimately be universal or single-arch; list whatever
          # was built rather than assuming a key that may not exist, because a
          # manifest pointing at a missing key silently disables updates for
          # that platform.
          def entry(payload_glob, sig_glob, where, required=True):
              """One (payload, signature) pair, scoped to one artifact dir.

              Scoping matters now there are two macOS artifacts: both payloads
              are called Teletype.app.tar.gz, so an unscoped glob picks one at
              random and can attach the arm64 signature to the x86_64 download.

              `required=False` downgrades a missing signature to a warning and
              returns None. That is for the best-effort Intel job only: its
              `continue-on-error` means a partial artifact must not be able to
              stop the arm64 and Windows release from shipping. A missing
              signature on a *required* platform stays fatal, because the
              updater cannot verify that download.
              """
              payloads = sorted(glob.glob(f"{where}/**/{payload_glob}", recursive=True))
              if not payloads:
                  if required:
                      raise SystemExit(f"no {payload_glob} under {where}")
                  print(f"::warning::{where} has no {payload_glob}; skipping it.")
                  return None
              if len(payloads) > 1:
                  raise SystemExit(
                      f"{where} holds {len(payloads)} {payload_glob} payloads: "
                      f"{payloads}. Cannot choose one; refusing to guess."
                  )
              payload = payloads[0]
              sigs = sorted(glob.glob(f"{where}/**/{sig_glob}", recursive=True))
              if not sigs:
                  if required:
                      raise SystemExit(f"payload {payload} has no signature at {sig_glob}")
                  print(
                      f"::warning::{payload} has no signature; skipping this "
                      "platform rather than publishing an unverifiable download."
                  )
                  return None
              return {
                  "signature": os.path.basename(sigs[0]),
                  "url": f"{base}/{os.path.basename(payload)}",
                  "size": os.path.getsize(payload),
              }

          def arch_of(artifact):
              """The architecture the build job recorded for its own binary.

              Read from a marker file written by the job that compiled the
              binary, not from a filename or a guess. Without it, a
              `darwin-x86_64` entry can point at an arm64 payload: the signature
              is a genuine signature over the arm64 tarball, so it verifies, the
              app installs, and then refuses to launch on the Intel Mac that
              asked for it. An Intel Mac with no entry at all just never gets an
              update, which is a much smaller failure.
              """
              marker = sorted(glob.glob(f"dist/{artifact}/**/ARCH", recursive=True))
              if not marker:
                  return None
              with open(marker[0]) as fh:
                  return fh.read().strip()

          if not os.path.isdir("dist/macos-release"):
              raise SystemExit("the arm64 macOS artifact is missing from dist/")

          mac_arch = arch_of("macos-release")
          if mac_arch != "aarch64":
              raise SystemExit(
                  f"macos-release reports arch {mac_arch!r}, expected 'aarch64'. "
                  "Refusing to publish a manifest that could point at the wrong "
                  "binary."
              )
          mac = entry("*.app.tar.gz", "*.app.tar.gz.sig", "dist/macos-release", required=False)
          if mac:
              platforms["darwin-aarch64"] = mac
          else:
              print("::notice::arm64 macOS payload present but unsigned; "
                    "darwin-aarch64 not advertised in the updater manifest this "
                    "release. The .app/.dmg assets still ship; in-app updates "
                    "for this platform are unavailable until a signing key is "
                    "added.")

          # Intel is optional: the job is `continue-on-error`, so on a day when
          # the x86_64 build breaks, this branch is simply skipped and arm64 and
          # Windows users are unaffected.
          if os.path.isdir("dist/macos-release-intel"):
              intel_arch = arch_of("macos-release-intel")
              if intel_arch != "x86_64":
                  raise SystemExit(
                      f"macos-release-intel reports arch {intel_arch!r}, expected "
                      "'x86_64'. Refusing to advertise it under darwin-x86_64."
                  )
              intel = entry(
                  "*.app.tar.gz", "*.app.tar.gz.sig", "dist/macos-release-intel",
                  required=False,
              )
              if intel:
                  platforms["darwin-x86_64"] = intel
                  print("advertising darwin-x86_64 from the Intel build")
              else:
                  print("::notice::Intel artifact present but unusable/unsigned; "
                        "darwin-x86_64 not advertised this release.")
          else:
              print("::warning::No Intel macOS artifact. Intel Macs will not be "
                    "offered an update this release.")

          win = entry("*.nsis.zip", "*.nsis.zip.sig", "dist/windows-release", required=False)
          if win:
              platforms["windows-x86_64"] = win
          else:
              print("::notice::Windows payload present but unsigned; "
                    "windows-x86_64 not advertised in the updater manifest this "
                    "release. The .exe asset still ships; in-app updates for "
                    "this platform are unavailable until a signing key is added.")

          if not platforms and not (not key_present and allow):
              # F-04: an updater manifest that offers nothing is a hard failure,
              # not a warning. A release whose manifest carries zero platforms
              # cannot be "latest" for anybody, so it must not publish.
              print("::error::Updater manifest would contain zero platforms. Refusing to publish an update that offers nothing.")
              raise SystemExit(1)

          if not platforms:
              # ALLOW_NO_UPDATER=true is the explicit operator override for an
              # unsigned release: publish it as a pre-release with the
              # zero-platform manifest, which disables in-app updates.
              print("::warning::ALLOW_NO_UPDATER=true: publishing unsigned, with a zero-platform updater manifest (in-app updates disabled).")

          manifest = {
              "version": version,
              "notes": f"v{version}",
              # The updater plugin (tauri-plugin-updater 2.x) treats a missing
              # or empty pub_date as "no update available" and never offers the
              # download, so this field is load-bearing. The tauri signer
              # stamps it with the build time; here the tag push time is the
              # honest equivalent.
              "pub_date": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(
                  "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
              ),
              "platforms": platforms,
          }
          with open("latest.json", "w") as fh:
              json.dump(manifest, fh, indent=2)
          print(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
          PY
      - name: Check the macOS payloads actually exist
        # `action-gh-release` treats a glob that matches nothing as success.
        # That is the whole reason a `.app` could sit in the build artifact for
        # a release and never reach the page: `.app` is a directory, the glob
        # matched no *file*, and the job stayed green. v0.2.2 shipped a DMG and
        # an installer and no app bundle, and nothing in CI noticed.
        #
        # So assert on the thing the user is meant to download, before the
        # upload, rather than trusting a glob. arm64 macOS and Windows are
        # required jobs; Intel is `continue-on-error`, so it is reported rather
        # than required.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # `find`, not a shell glob: bash without `globstar` reads `**` as a
          # single `*`, so `dist/**/*.dmg` would not match the real
          # `dist/macos-release/dmg/Teletype_0.2.2_aarch64.dmg`. The
          # action-gh-release `files:` list below is matched by
          # @actions/glob, which does understand `**`; a shell does not.
          n_zip=$(find dist -type f -name '*.app.zip' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          n_dmg=$(find dist -type f -name '*.dmg' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          n_exe=$(find dist -type f -name '*.exe' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          echo "app.zip=$n_zip dmg=$n_dmg exe=$n_exe"
          find dist -type f \( -name '*.app.zip' -o -name '*.dmg' -o -name '*.exe' \) \
            -exec sh -c 'echo "    $1"' _ {} \;
          fail=0
          [ "$n_zip" -ge 1 ] || { echo "::error::no macOS .app.zip was built or uploaded"; fail=1; }
          [ "$n_dmg" -ge 1 ] || { echo "::error::no macOS .dmg was built or uploaded"; fail=1; }
          [ "$n_exe" -ge 1 ] || { echo "::error::no Windows .exe was built or uploaded"; fail=1; }
          if [ "$n_zip" -lt 2 ]; then
            echo "::warning::only $n_zip macOS app bundle(s) present; the x86_64 job is continue-on-error, so this is expected when it fails."
          fi
          if [ "$n_dmg" -lt 2 ]; then
            echo "::warning::only $n_dmg macOS dmg(s) present; the x86_64 job is continue-on-error, so this is expected when it fails."
          fi
          [ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
      - name: Check release asset names are unique
        # A duplicate name means one architecture silently does not ship, and
        # the manifest would advertise a download that resolves to the other
        # one. Cheap to check, and the failure mode is otherwise invisible.
        #
        # `-name '*.app'` is gone: a `.app` is a directory, so under `-type f`
        # it could never match anything and was dead weight in this check.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          find dist -type f \( -name '*.app.zip' -o -name '*.dmg' -o -name '*.exe' \
            -o -name '*.app.tar.gz' -o -name '*.app.tar.gz.sig' \
            -o -name '*.nsis.zip' -o -name '*.nsis.zip.sig' \) \
            -exec basename {} \; | sort | uniq -d | while read -r dup; do
            echo "::error::two release assets are both named '$dup'"
            find dist -name "$dup" -exec echo "    {}" \;
            exit 1
          done
          echo "asset names are unique"
      - name: Publish GitHub Release
        # F-05/F-04: publish as a pre-release first, and only let the
        # verify-release job promote to "latest" after it passes. Nothing is
        # ever "latest" before the published manifest has been verified.
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          generate_release_notes: true
          make_latest: false
          prerelease: true
          files: |
            dist/**/*.app.zip
            dist/**/*.dmg
            dist/**/*.exe
            dist/**/*.app.tar.gz
            dist/**/*.app.tar.gz.sig
            dist/**/*.nsis.zip
            dist/**/*.nsis.zip.sig
            latest.json

[package]
name = "teletype-desktop"
description = "Teletype desktop app (Tauri 2)"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true

[lib]
name = "teletype_desktop_lib"
crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]

[[bin]]
name = "teletype"
path = "src/main.rs"

[features]
default = ["neudecide"]
# HARD-3: test-only fault injector. Off by default; a release build (and a
# plain `cargo test`) must not contain the injector or its injection points.
# Enable with `--features fault-injection` to run the edge-case matrix tests.
fault-injection = []
# Exposes `tauri::test::mock_app()` so the dictation controller's
# concurrency tests can build a Session without a real Tauri app.
test = ["tauri/test", "teletype-core/test-support"]
# NeuDecide decider in command mode (Addendum A). Default ON as of
# 2026-10-18 (A.5 flip: parity 92% ≥ 90%, suite +24.9 ≥ +20, latency
# p95 87.5 ms under the user-approved 200 ms budget). Pulls the ONNX
# runtime into the decider; when the model files are absent at runtime
# the take-level selection falls through to Needle (A.3.3 wiring).
neudecide = ["teletype-decider/onnx"]

[build-dependencies]
tauri-build = { version = "2", features = [] }
cc = "1"

[dev-dependencies]
tempfile = "3"
proptest = "1"

[dependencies]
teletype-catalog = { path = "../teletype-catalog" }
teletype-core = { path = "../teletype-core", features = ["test-support"] }
teletype-decider = { path = "../teletype-decider" }
teletype-speech = { path = "../teletype-speech" }
teletype-fluid = { path = "../teletype-fluid" }
teletype-apple = { path = "../teletype-apple" }
teletype-inference = { path = "../teletype-inference" }
silero-vad-pure = { version = "0.1.1", default-features = false }
tauri = { version = "2", features = ["tray-icon", "image-png", "macos-private-api", "devtools"] }
tauri-plugin-global-shortcut = "2"
tauri-plugin-opener = "2.5"
tauri-plugin-dialog = "2"
# In-app updates. Tauri 2 has this built in, so it is cross-platform and reuses
# the existing app shell rather than adding a second update framework.
tauri-plugin-updater = "2"
# Required by the updater to relaunch the app after installing an update.
tauri-plugin-process = "2"
# One process per login session. Every process installs its own global
# shortcut listeners and typing tap during setup, so a second launch means a
# second set of listeners and dictation is typed twice. The plugin hands the
# new process's argv to the running instance and exits it. 2.5.x is the line
# built against tauri 2.12 and rustc 1.90 (2.4.x still requires tauri ^2.10).
tauri-plugin-single-instance = "2.5"
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
thiserror = { workspace = true }
arc-swap = { workspace = true }
tracing = { workspace = true }
cpal = { workspace = true }
arboard = { workspace = true }
enigo = { workspace = true }
uuid = { workspace = true }
dirs = { workspace = true }
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["rustls-tls", "blocking", "json"] }
# Parses the user-supplied provider base URL. Hand-rolled splitting on
# `:` and `/` mistook URL userinfo for the host (see read_api_key).
url = "2"
# Streams the SHA-256 of a downloaded model file without holding it in memory.
sha2 = "0.10"
# Sherpa-onnx speech models ship as `.tar.bz2` release archives and are
# extracted into their provider directory on install.
tar = "0.4"
bzip2 = "0.5"
keyring = "4"
# SIGTERM signal handling: tao 0.37 does not translate SIGTERM into a Tauri
# RunEvent on macOS, so a `kill <pid>` (or a launchd/systemd stop) killed the
# app with Rust's default terminate action, orphans the llama-server, and left
# a stale pid file behind. We install a handler that requests an orderly exit
# through the same RunEvent::Exit teardown the tray Quit uses.
libc = "0.2"
# Pure-Rust audio decoder for file transcription (P3.17): wav/mp3/flac/ogg/aac.
symphonia = "0.5"

[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
objc2 = { version = "0.6", features = ["catch-all"] }
objc2-foundation = { version = "0.3", features = ["NSString"] }
core-foundation = "0.10"
# Pre-generated Accessibility bindings for the direct-write injection tier.
# The AX headers ship only in the full Xcode SDK; these compile against the
# Command Line Tools SDK, which is what CI and a fresh checkout use.
objc2-application-services = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = [
    "AXError",
    "AXUIElement",
    "AXValue",
    "AXValueConstants",
    "HIServices",
    "objc2-foundation",
] }
objc2-core-foundation = { version = "0.3", features = ["CFString"] }
# CoreAudio transport-type detection for smart mic selection (plan §5.2).
# Already in the workspace dependency tree via cpal; used on macOS only for
# kAudioDevicePropertyTransportType.
coreaudio-rs = "0.14"
objc2-core-audio = "0.3"
# Apple Intelligence system model (P1.4): on-device, zero-download polish/LLM
# provider. Statically links the FoundationModels framework and needs a Swift
# bridge + the macOS 26 SDK, so it is target-gated to macOS: an un-gated copy
# broke the windows-latest CI job (D007) and was reverted (L048). Keep it gated.
foundation-models = "0.12"

[target.'cfg(target_os = "windows")'.dependencies.windows]
version = "0.61"
features = [
  "Win32_Foundation",
  "Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging",
  "Win32_System_Threading",
  "Win32_System_ProcessStatus",
  "Win32_System_LibraryLoader",
  # F-24: --self-test attaches to the parent console in a GUI-subsystem build.
  "Win32_System_Console",
  # P8.5: UIA property reads return `VARIANT` (Win32_Sub-Variant); the
  # `GetCurrentPropertyValue` family is cfg-gated on Com+Ole+Variant and the
  # Variant helpers (VariantToBoolean/VariantToInt32/VariantToStringAlloc) on
  # Com+Ole. Verified against the 0.61.3 source cfg attributes.
  "Win32_System_Com",
  "Win32_System_Ole",
  "Win32_System_Variant",
  # P8.5: UIA readers (focused control text, selection, caret context).
  # In windows-rs 0.61 the UIA COM API lives in `Win32::UI::Accessibility`
  # (there is no `Win32::UI::Automation` module); verified against
  # windows-0.61.3/src/Windows/Win32/UI/Accessibility/mod.rs and gated by
  # the `Win32_UI_Accessibility` feature (windows-0.61.3/Cargo.toml:703).
  "Win32_UI_Accessibility",
  # P8.5: start/stop dictation cues via PlaySoundW. In 0.61 PlaySoundW and
  # the SND_* flags live in `Win32::Media::Audio` (verified against
  # windows-0.61.3/src/Windows/Win32/Media/Audio/mod.rs), not in
  # `Win32::System::Diagnostics::Debug`.
  "Win32_Media_Audio",
]

[lints]
workspace = true
